title: One finite quotient detects formal maps with a torsion comparison
statement: For X Noetherian and J an ideal, let b:Q→R be a coherent arrow whose kernel T is killed by a positive power of J. Suppose T→Q/J^(n+1)Q is monomorphic. For any coherent formal module M and formal maps f,g:M→Q^, equality f≫b^=g≫b^ and equality f_n=g_n at level n+1 imply f=g. Formal modules and completion are those of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module].

source.place: Tag 0889(1), affine comparison and uniqueness; Tags 05EK and 088A

proof.text: Restrict to an affine open and apply the affine equivalence to interpret the formal maps as maps of finite completed modules.
Exactness of completion identifies ker(b^) with T^. Since J^s T=0, the canonical completion map identifies T^ with T. The prescribed separating quotient is injective on that kernel.

The difference f−g has image in this kernel by the composition equation. Its n-th component is zero, so injectivity of T→Q/J^(n+1)Q kills the difference. Transport back to the affine formal systems, then check equality locally on an affine cover at every component.

theorem formalMap_torsion_finite_detection
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (Q R : CoherentModules X) (b : Q ⟶ R)
    (hker : ∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
        (kernel b.hom)))
    (n : ℕ) (hsep : Mono (kernel.ι b.hom ≫ formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) Q.obj))
    (M : CoherentFormalModule X J) (f g : M ⟶ (completion X J).obj Q)
    (hcomp : f ≫ (completion X J).map b = g ≫ (completion X J).map b)
    (hlevel : f.hom.app (op n) = g.hom.app (op n)) : f = g
